item.title: BREAKING: Sheriff's Investigation Finds No Stabbing at Jamie Foxx's SKVLK Fest
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: It's official. Ventura County detectives say the teen at Anelise's 18th birthday festival "was not assaulted with a knife." Read the full press release. Did you believe the stabbing story?
item.content:encoded:
BreakingOfficialPress Release

BREAKING: Sheriff's Investigation Finds No Stabbing at Jamie Foxx's SKVLK Fest

It's official. Ventura County detectives say the teen at Anelise's 18th birthday festival "was not assaulted with a knife." Read the full press release, and the reports that got it wrong. Did you believe the stabbing story?

By Hollywood News Access · November 11, 2026

There was no stabbing. The Ventura County Sheriff's Office has confirmed it.

For three days, headlines said a teenager was slashed with a knife at Jamie Foxx's home during SKVLK Fest, the Halloween music festival his daughter Anelise threw for her 18th birthday. Now detectives have interviewed the young man and found he "was not assaulted with a knife." His superficial injury, the Sheriff says, appears to be from "mutual combat / simple battery."

The festival has issued its official release. Here it is in full.

Press release · For immediate release

Sheriff’s Investigation Finds No Stabbing at Jamie Foxx’s SKVLK Fest Halloween Party

The Ventura County Sheriff’s Office investigated and confirmed that no one was stabbed, contrary to widespread media reports.

HIDDEN VALLEY, Calif. (November 10, 2026) — The Ventura County Sheriff's Office investigated and confirmed that no one was stabbed at the November 7th SKVLK Fest Halloween party at Jamie Foxx’s Hidden Valley home, contrary to widespread media reports.

Early reports to Sheriff’s dispatch alleged that one juvenile had slashed another with a knife, and those initial claims were repeated widely in the press. On November 9th, detectives interviewed the victim and determined the victim was not assaulted with a knife and that the superficial injury appears to have resulted from a mutual combat/simple battery.

“We’re grateful to the Ventura County Sheriff's deputies and detectives for their thorough work, and to the EMTs and security staff who responded quickly that night,” the festival said in a statement issued through PR STARPOWER, which leads sponsorships and partnerships for SKVLK Fest. “Our thoughts are with everyone who was hurt, and we’re cooperating fully as the investigations continue. But the record needs to be clear: no one was stabbed. We hope the outlets that reported otherwise will correct their stories.”

The Sheriff’s Office is continuing to investigate the separate altercations that occurred that night. Mr. Foxx’s team is cooperating fully and encourages anyone with video of those incidents to share it with the Sheriff’s East County Investigations Bureau.

We urge media outlets that reported a stabbing to update their coverage to reflect the Sheriff’s findings.

Media contact: PR STARPOWER Media Relations · info@prstarpower.com

###

What the Sheriff found

Deputies were called to the Hidden Valley home on the night of Saturday, Nov. 7, after early reports that one juvenile had slashed another. That first account is what spread. On Monday, Nov. 9, detectives interviewed the young man, and the knife story fell apart. The Sheriff's release (RB# 26-146404) also describes two other altercations that night, which detectives are still investigating.

The party everyone is talking about

Strip away the false headline and here's what SKVLK Fest actually was: carnival rides glowing until late, a packed main stage and thousands of young people celebrating Anelise's 18th. Organizers say more than 400 security guards worked the night and shuttle buses moved guests in and out. Read our exclusive: the love behind the fest.

At a glance

The claim
A teen was stabbed or slashed at SKVLK Fest (widely reported Nov. 8–9)
The finding
"Not assaulted with a knife"; superficial injury from "mutual combat / simple battery" (Ventura County Sheriff)
Still under investigation
Two separate altercations the same night
Sources
Sheriff's release · Official release

What's next: the festival's team has asked every outlet that ran the stabbing claim to correct it. We'll track who does. Did you see the original headline? Tell us where.

Disclosure: Hollywood News Access is part of the same media group as PR STARPOWER, which represents SKVLK Fest. Terry Bryant of PR STARPOWER is a senior editor in the group.

item.title: 400 Guards, Shuttle Buses and a Lot of Happy Kids: The Love Behind Jamie Foxx's SKVLK Fest
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Parents brought their children, the kids rode the rides until late, and families went home grateful. Inside the care Jamie Foxx and his team put into Anelise's 18th birthday festival. Were you there?
item.content:encoded:
ExclusiveFeel-GoodHollywood News Access

400 Guards, Shuttle Buses and a Lot of Happy Kids: The Love Behind Jamie Foxx's SKVLK Fest

Parents brought their children, the kids rode the rides until late, and families went home grateful. Inside the care Jamie Foxx and his team put into Anelise's 18th birthday festival. Were you there?

By Hollywood News Access · November 11, 2026

Before the first beat dropped, the buses were already rolling.

When Jamie Foxx and his daughter Anelise opened their Hidden Valley home for SKVLK Fest, her 18th birthday Halloween festival, they weren't just throwing a party. They were hosting thousands of families. And by every account Hollywood News Access gathered on the ground and in the days since, they took that seriously.

The numbers behind the night

Organizers say more than 400 security guards worked the festival. Shuttle buses carried guests in and out, so families weren't left hunting for parking on dark hillside roads. EMTs were on site and, the festival's team says, responded quickly when needed.

That's the part of the story that didn't trend. It should have.

The kids had the night of their lives

Picture it: a carnival ride flashing green, red and pink against the night sky, kids screaming and laughing as it spun. Costumes everywhere. A main stage lit like a stadium, with thousands of hands in the air. Friends filming each other, and everyone singing along.

Many parents came with their children, and plenty of teens arrived with friends to celebrate one of their own turning 18.

Parents noticed

Parents who spoke with Hollywood News Access said they were grateful, both for the night itself and for how their children were looked after. The word that came up again and again was care.

"Jamie and his team genuinely care about the children," said Terry Bryant of PR STARPOWER, which brought sponsors and partners to SKVLK Fest. "There was an outpouring of support and love from the community, and the parents were so grateful. With more than 400 security guards and buses for the families, they really led, and they should be commended for that."

And the record

A false report that a teen was stabbed overshadowed all of this for days. The Ventura County Sheriff's Office has now confirmed no one was stabbed; the young man "was not assaulted with a knife." Detectives are still looking into two separate altercations that night, and the festival's team says it is cooperating fully. Read the breaking story and the official release.

At a glance

SKVLK Fest 2026, Anelise's 18th birthday Halloween festival
When
Saturday, November 7, 2026
Where
The Foxx family home, Hidden Valley (Thousand Oaks area)
Security
More than 400 guards, according to organizers
Getting there
Shuttle buses for guests, according to organizers
Crowd
More than 25,000 per organizers; 3,000 or more per the Sheriff's Office

item.title: Usher and Chris Brown Cancel Their November 16 SoFi Show as Feud Reports Swirl
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Ticketmaster now reads CANCELED for the R&B Tour's second Los Angeles night, and Miami is gone too. TMZ says the trouble started backstage in Atlanta. Refund or hold out for a makeup date?
item.content:encoded:
MusicTour dramaHollywood News Access

Usher and Chris Brown Cancel Their November 16 SoFi Show as Feud Reports Swirl

Ticketmaster now reads CANCELED for the R&B Tour's second Los Angeles night, and Miami is gone too. TMZ says the trouble started backstage in Atlanta. Refund or hold out for a makeup date?

By Hollywood News Access · November 11, 2026

One night in Inglewood is still on. The other one is gone.

Usher and Chris Brown have canceled the Monday, November 16 stop of their R&B Tour at SoFi Stadium, TMZ reported, citing a ticket holder's Ticketmaster account that now marks the show "CANCELED." Fans are being told they will be refunded.

The November 15 SoFi show is still on, according to TMZ.

Miami is out too

The December 6 date at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami has also been scrapped, TheGrio and Complex reported. Ticketmaster gives no reason for either cancellation, and neither singer has said anything publicly.

What reportedly happened in Atlanta

This part is reporting, not confirmed fact. According to TMZ's sources, the two argued backstage at their Atlanta show last week: Usher wanted to start on time, and Brown wanted to hold the show for fans stuck in traffic. IBTimes UK, citing unnamed sources, said the show started nearly three hours late.

It is not the tour's first cut. In October, four shows came off the schedule (Baltimore, Cincinnati, Columbia and Indianapolis), with the promoter citing the well-being of the touring party and crew, FOX5 Las Vegas reported.

What's still on

TheGrio reports the remaining dates in Atlanta, New Orleans, Houston and Tampa appear unaffected for now.

At a glance

Canceled
SoFi Stadium, Inglewood, Monday Nov 16 (TMZ); Hard Rock Stadium, Miami, Sunday Dec 6 (TheGrio, Complex)
Still on
SoFi Stadium, Sunday Nov 15
Refunds
Ticket holders are being told they will be refunded
Reason given
None on Ticketmaster
The feud
Reported by TMZ, unconfirmed by either singer
Earlier cuts
Baltimore, Cincinnati, Columbia, Indianapolis (October)

If you had tickets for the 16th, check your email for the refund. Are you going on the 15th, or is the magic gone?

Listen while you wait: Usher's Confessions on Amazon. Shopping links may earn Hollywood News Access a commission.

Reporting drawn from TMZ, TheGrio, Complex, IBTimes UK and FOX5 Las Vegas. Feud details are as reported by those outlets. Written independently by Hollywood News Access in our own words.

item.title: Janet Jackson Surprises Jenna Dewan on DWTS, Then Dewan Goes Home One Step From the Semifinals
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Her old boss sent a video message. Dewan danced to "All for You," scored 28 out of 30, and still got cut on Grammy Night. Robbed?
item.content:encoded:
TV & StreamingDWTSHollywood News Access

Janet Jackson Surprises Jenna Dewan on DWTS, Then Dewan Goes Home One Step From the Semifinals

Her old boss sent a video message. Dewan danced to "All for You," scored 28 out of 30, and still got cut on Grammy Night. Robbed?

By Hollywood News Access · November 11, 2026

Jenna Dewan got a message from Janet Jackson on Tuesday night. A few minutes later, she got the bad news.

On the Grammy Night episode of Dancing With the Stars, Janet Jackson sent a rare video message to her former backup dancer, wishing Jenna Dewan luck and saying she couldn't wait to watch, E! News reported.

Dewan danced in Jackson's "Doesn't Really Matter" and "All for You" videos early in her career. On Tuesday she and pro partner Val Chmerkovskiy danced a jazz routine to "All for You."

The score, then the shock

The judges gave them 28 out of 30, according to E!. The Hollywood Reporter says that made them the night's second-best scoring couple.

It didn't save them. Dewan and Chmerkovskiy were eliminated, the last couple out before the semifinals, E! and Page Six reported. Page Six called it the most shocking elimination yet.

A stacked night

Grammy Night also brought live performances from Sheryl Crow, Maren Morris, and Brandy and Monica, TheWrap reported. Brandy and Monica used the moment to announce their first Las Vegas residency.

The takeawayFrom Janet's dancer to Janet's shout-out, on national TV. Some exits still feel like wins.

item.title: Florence Pugh's New Set Rules: 'Show Up on Time, Don't Be Rude, Don't Be a Misogynist'
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: The East of Eden star says she is done tolerating bad behavior at work, especially toward the crew. Should every call sheet carry her three rules?
item.content:encoded:
CelebritySpeaking outHollywood News Access

Florence Pugh's New Set Rules: 'Show Up on Time, Don't Be Rude, Don't Be a Misogynist'

The East of Eden star says she is done tolerating bad behavior at work, especially toward the crew. Should every call sheet carry her three rules?

By Hollywood News Access · November 11, 2026

Florence Pugh has three rules for the people she works with. Break one and she will say something.

In a new Elle interview, Pugh said her confidence has grown film by film, and that she now refuses to put up with bad behavior on set. Her standard, as quoted by Variety: "Show up on time, don't be rude, don't be a misogynist."

The crew comes first

Pugh said she is "not allowing for people to be rude to the crew," according to Variety's account of the interview. She described a set's mood as something everyone can sense: "the moment someone is making that vibe feel off, everybody feels it."

She has become "more confident in the way that I can protect myself" working in Hollywood, The Hollywood Reporter reported.

Florence's rulesShow up on time. Don't be rude. Don't be a misogynist.

Why people are listening

Pugh is one of the busiest actors of her generation: an Oscar nominee for Little Women, a lead in Oppenheimer and Marvel's Thunderbolts*, and now Cathy Ames in Netflix's East of Eden, the character Netflix's Tudum cover story calls the show's most complex. When a star at that level says the crew deserves respect, producers notice.

Who
Florence Pugh

Her rules

Pugh's rules are simple. Why do so many sets still need them spelled out?

item.title: Inside SKVLK Fest 2026: Anelise's 18th Birthday Bash Was the Party of the Year
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Carnival rides, a stacked lineup and a VIP creator lounge: Jamie Foxx and his daughter Anelise threw Thousand Oaks a night to remember. And the stabbing story? The festival's team says it never happened. Were you there?
item.content:encoded:
CelebrityParty of the YearHollywood News Access

Inside SKVLK Fest 2026: Anelise's 18th Birthday Bash Was the Party of the Year

Carnival rides, a stacked lineup and a VIP creator lounge: Jamie Foxx and his daughter Anelise threw Thousand Oaks a night to remember. And the stabbing story? The festival's team says it never happened. Were you there?

By Hollywood News Access · November 10, 2026

Some kids get a cake for their 18th. Anelise got a festival. SKVLK Fest, the Halloween music festival she created, took over the family's Thousand Oaks home on Saturday night, and with her dad Jamie Foxx behind her, it was the party everybody wanted to be at.

Think carnival rides, a glowing main stage, red carpet entrances and a VIP creator lounge styled by Dolls Kill, where creators filmed their looks and went live all night. Entertainment Weekly reported a lineup including Offset, OhGeesy, 310babii and SuperDuperKyle. Organizers say more than 25,000 people came through; the Sheriff's Office estimated 3,000 or more.

"It was amazing," said Terry Matari Bryant of PR STARPOWER, the festival's publicist, who was there all night. "The community loved it, the young people loved it, and Jamie and Anelise put on a fantastic show."

Jamie Foxx clearly agreed: he posted videos from the night praising his daughter.

About that stabbing story

By Sunday, TMZ was reporting, citing law enforcement sources, that a guest had been stabbed, and the story spread fast. The festival's team says it is false. "No one was stabbed," PR STARPOWER said in an official statement. Two teenagers had a brief scuffle, one got a minor scratch, and Ventura County deputies responded, according to the statement. Update, Nov. 10: the Ventura County Sheriff's Office now confirms it. Detectives spoke to the young man and "determined the victim was not assaulted with a knife," the Sheriff's release says; the injury appears to be from "mutual combat / simple battery." The release also describes two other altercations that night, which remain under investigation. The team has asked every outlet that ran the stabbing claim to correct it. Read the Sheriff's release · Read the statement.

item.content:encoded:
Red carpetTonightHollywood News Access

Richard T. Jones Hosts Hollywood's Most Global Red Carpet Tonight

DeVon Franklin, Oscar winner Nick Vallelonga and Grammy-nominated producer Theron “Neff-U” Feemster lead filmmakers from 30 nations into the Writers Guild Theater. Who are you hoping to see on the carpet?

By Hollywood News Access · November 5, 2026

Beverly Hills gets a passport stamp tonight. The 2026 Global Film Awards roll out the red carpet at 5 PM at the Writers Guild Theater on South Doheny Drive, and the man running the show is Richard T. Jones, the Sgt. Wade Grey of ABC’s The Rookie.

The guest list mixes Hollywood power with first-time filmmakers. DeVon Franklin, the producer and bestselling author behind Franklin Entertainment, leads the arrivals with Nick Vallelonga, who won two Oscars for Green Book. Actress and singer Demetria McKinney, Grammy-nominated producer Theron “Neff-U” Feemster, Ricco Ross, Richard Lawson and Zambian gospel artist Ephriam Mutalangue are also on the list.

950 films, 30 countries, one carpet

The Authentic Global Film Festival says more than 950 films from roughly 30 countries were submitted this year. Many of the filmmakers walking tonight have never seen their work on a big screen. That is the point, says founder Dr. Gershom Sikaala: “Talent doesn’t depend on where you were born or how old you are, but opportunity too often does.”

What to watch for

At 6 PM, Vallelonga, Franklin and Feemster sit down for a panel hosted by Anabelle D. Munro, with filmmaker Amanda “Kazzy” Cryer and producer Joey Zhou. The awards run from 7 to 9 PM, and the party moves to N10 on West 3rd Street at 10 PM. We’re on the carpet all night, so follow @hollywoodnewsaccess for arrivals as they happen.

item.title: Hollywood Celebrates the Blue Wave
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: From Jimmy Kimmel's late-night victory lap to John Leguizamo's “this is redemption time,” the stars came out for the Democrats' midterm sweep, and the history-makers gave them plenty to cheer.
item.content:encoded:
Election 2026Celebrity reactionHollywood News Access

Hollywood Celebrates the Blue Wave

From Jimmy Kimmel's late-night victory lap to John Leguizamo's “this is redemption time,” the stars came out for the Democrats' midterm sweep, and the history-makers gave them plenty to cheer.

By Hollywood News Access · November 4, 2026

UPDATED Nov. 5: It's official in Georgia. Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governor's race after Republican Rick Jackson conceded, the first Black woman ever elected governor of a U.S. state. Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are still too close to call.

Hollywood stayed up late on Tuesday, and it was worth it. Democrats won control of the House and seized a Senate majority in the 2026 midterms, and the entertainment world reacted like it was awards night.

Jimmy Kimmel was the first late-night host to take on the results, taping later than usual so he could mock President Trump over the losses, The Hollywood Reporter reported. John Leguizamo summed up the mood in four words: "This is redemption time."

Who was celebrating

Bette Midler and Viola Davis were among the stars cheering the results, along with Alyssa Milano, Molly Ringwald, Stephen Colbert, Mandy Moore and Henry Winkler, according to The Hollywood Reporter and Billboard. Even James Woods, one of Trump's loudest supporters in town, reportedly congratulated the Democrats.

The mood in HollywoodRedemption time. Billboard's headline put it simply: "Dreams do come true."

The history-makers

The night gave the stars plenty to celebrate. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governor's race, becoming the first Black woman ever elected governor of a U.S. state. In Texas, James Talarico became the first Democrat the state has sent to the Senate since 1988, and Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott. In Kansas, pastor Adam Hamilton became the first Democratic senator from the state since 1932.

And at home, California elected Xavier Becerra as its first Latino governor.

Election night at a glance

House
Democrats win control
Senate
Democrats take a majority
Georgia
Keisha Lance Bottoms wins, a historic first
Texas
Talarico to the Senate; Hinojosa beats Abbott
California
Xavier Becerra elected governor
Still counting
Alaska and Mississippi Senate races, some House seats

Reporting drawn from The Hollywood Reporter, Billboard, NBC News, CBS News and the Associated Press. Results are preliminary.

item.title: Ramayana Takes Over the Academy Museum
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi brought Indian cinema's most anticipated epic to a Los Angeles red carpet on Tuesday night, and the fans outside chanted for the villain.
item.content:encoded:
Red carpetPremiereHollywood News Access

Ramayana Takes Over the Academy Museum

Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi brought Indian cinema's most anticipated epic to a Los Angeles red carpet on Tuesday night, and the fans outside chanted for the villain.

By Hollywood News Access · October 29, 2026

Hollywood's own museum rolled out the carpet for Bollywood on Tuesday night. Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, one of the most anticipated films in Indian cinema, held its Los Angeles premiere on October 27 at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures, with an invite-only 3D screening of the English-language version in the museum's David Geffen Theatre.

All three leads showed up. Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Ram, walked the carpet with Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita. Yash, the film's Ravana, arrived with his wife, actress Radhika Pandit. Director Nitesh Tiwari, filmmaker Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra were with them, and Jada Pinkett Smith was among the Hollywood guests.

The fans picked a side

The crowd outside made the loudest noise of the night, and not all of it was for the hero. Fans chanted "Ravana" as Yash came down the carpet, called "RK" when Ranbir arrived, and broke into "Jai Shri Ram" as the cast posed. Videos of the arrivals went viral in India within hours.

The leads came dressed for the occasion, in traditional Indian wear rather than standard premiere black tie.

Why Los Angeles

A world premiere at the Academy's own museum is a statement. Indian studios have been courting the American market for years, and Tuesday's guest list put the film in front of the people who vote on, program and distribute movies in this town.

item.title: Freda Payne Stole VMAs Weekend
item.dc:creator: By Hollywood News Access
item.description: Every camera in town was pointed at the Peacock Theater. But the night Hollywood can't stop raving about happened on Sunset, where an 84-year-old legend in gold lamé delivered a sold-out, standing-ovation, once-in-a-lifetime triumph.
item.content:encoded:
Hollywood is ravingSold outReview

Freda Payne Stole VMAs Weekend

Every camera in town was pointed at the Peacock Theater. But the night Hollywood can't stop raving about happened on Sunset, where an 84-year-old legend in gold lamé delivered a sold-out, standing-ovation, once-in-a-lifetime triumph.

By Hollywood News Access · Photos by Terry Bryant · October 5, 2026

Forget the after-parties. The hottest ticket in Los Angeles on VMAs weekend did not come with a step-and-repeat. It came with a red velvet curtain, a jazz band dressed in gold, and Freda Payne.

The Detroit-born "Band of Gold" legend sold out Catalina Jazz Club on Saturday, September 26, with Freda Payne Portrays and Honors Legendary Ladies of Song. It was one week after her 84th birthday. She did not look it, she did not sing like it, and she did not slow down for a second.

Let's not bury the lede. This show was legendary. Standout. Stellar. Beyond outstanding. It was the kind of night people in this town will be bragging about having seen for years, and we were in the room.

The verdictA masterclass from a living legend. Freda Payne didn't just perform on Saturday night. She reigned.

Who was in the house

The star power in the room was off the charts. Stefanie Powers was there. Loretta Devine was there. And they were joined by a host of other celebrities, too many to name: screen stars, recording artists, producers, directors and Hollywood insiders, all packed into one sold-out room to see a legend at work.

On the biggest awards weekend of the fall, with every publicist in town working a carpet across the city, Hollywood picked a jazz club on Sunset. That says everything.

The finale: "Band of Gold"

And then she saved the best for last. Freda Payne closed the night with "Band of Gold," her own world-famous, chart-topping global hit, the song that made her an international star and has been played around the world ever since.

The room sang along. Then the room stood up. The standing ovation lasted three full minutes. Three minutes of a sold-out Hollywood crowd on its feet for a living legend. You do not see that every night, and you will not forget it once you have.

Two looks, zero misses

She opened in a gold lamé jumpsuit that caught every light in the room and every eye in the house. Then she came back in floor-length black lace with a thigh-high slit, as elegant as anything on a red carpet that weekend.

The moment

If you only hear about one number, make it "Fever." Peggy Lee's classic, sung in gold, two dancers at her side, red light pouring down the stage. She took her time with it. She let the bass walk. She owned every second of it. The room went wild. The applause came before the last note was finished, and it kept going long after it should have stopped. Simply sensational.

Nine legends, one star

The concept: Payne honored nine women who shaped American jazz and pop, many of whom she knew personally. Ella Fitzgerald, Sarah Vaughan, Dinah Washington, Lena Horne, Nancy Wilson, Peggy Lee, Gloria Lynne, Dakota Staton and Eartha Kitt.

She opened with Ella's "How High the Moon." She gave Sarah Vaughan "Body and Soul," Nancy Wilson "Guess Who I Saw Today," Gloria Lynne "I Wish You Love" and Dakota Staton "The Late Late Show." It was not a tribute act. It was a legend singing about the women she grew up watching, and you could hear every memory in it. The voice is still rich, still commanding, still pure Freda. Every song landed. Not one wasted moment.

Special guest: Thomasina Gross as Eartha Kitt

Special guest Thomasina Gross opened the evening as Eartha Kitt, in a leopard-print gown and black opera gloves, and set the mood beautifully. Her candlelit table scene, with two martinis and a gentleman caller, was a charming touch of old Hollywood.

It was the perfect warm-up for the main event. Because when Freda Payne walked out, the night belonged to her.

A family affair: Gregory Abbott Jr.

The night's host was Payne's son, Gregory Abbott Jr., and he was the perfect man for the job. Smooth, warm and quick, he kept the room laughing between numbers, and introduced the star of the night: his mother.

That introduction was a moment all by itself. A son calling his mother's name on Sunset Boulevard, and a sold-out house roaring for her. By the end of the night that same house was on its feet for three minutes straight. After the show the two of them posed together, him in electric-blue satin and her in a rose satin robe with feathered cuffs. Hollywood royalty, two generations deep.

Shout-out to Gregory Abbott Jr. He hosted like a pro, and the stage clearly runs in the family.

Take a bow, Donald B. Welch

A huge shout-out to the man who made it happen. Donald B. Welch, the playwright, director and producer behind the night, wrote and directed Legendary Ladies of Song and presented it under the Don B. Welch banner. The idea was his. So was the vision.

And what a vision. This was not a singer and a piano. It was a full production, with costume changes, scene work, actors and dancers, staged with the kind of care you usually only see in theater. Welch built a show around Freda Payne's memories of the women she grew up watching, gave her the room to shine, and filled every seat in the house.

A sold-out room on the busiest weekend of the fall is no accident. That is a producer who knows exactly what he is doing. Congratulations, Don. This one was a smash.

The band was gold, too

The musicians matched the star, dressed in gold: Josh Nelson on piano as musical director, Chris Colangelo on bass, Ricky Woodard on saxophone and Marcello Carelli on drums. Actors Terryl DaLuz and Kyrel Jaundoo filled out the stage.

What's next

Payne sets sail at the end of October with Holland America, performing on a cruise from Fort Lauderdale to Puerto Rico on a bill with Darlene Love and Wayne Newton.

As for Legendary Ladies of Song? It is built to tour. Producers, take note. Freda Payne is a national treasure, and on Saturday night she proved it all over again. If this show comes back around, buy the ticket the day it goes on sale. It sold out this time, and it will sell out faster next time.
